notes:
I found most of what you asked for, but there are gaps. I found nothing from netbible.org, bibleodyssey.org, oca.org/newadvent.org (Orthodox), Lutheran sites or seedbed.com. I also found no prosperity, word-of-faith or hyper-grace teaching on this chapter, so those are left out. I hit my tool limit before I could read the Pulpit Commentary or the full Preceptaustin page.

Some sources I read as whole pages, so I've listed their links without quotation tags: Enduring Word (https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/), Jimmy Akin at Catholic Answers (https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/the-woman-of-revelation-12) and Ligonier (https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman). The Enduring Word page cut off partway through v. 9.

**The main split, which runs through the whole chapter.** Teachers read the chapter in four different ways:
- **Future events (dispensational):** Guzik, Larkin, GotQuestions and Preceptaustin place most of it in a coming seven-year Tribulation. In this reading the woman is Israel.
- **Church history (historicist):** Wesley maps it onto events in church history.
- **The whole church age (Reformed):** Ligonier reads it as the time between Christ's two comings.
- **Catholic:** the woman stands for several things, including Mary.

---

**v. 1**
- **Israel (dispensational):** Guzik says this "sign" is not a literal woman. The sun, moon and twelve stars echo Joseph's dream in Genesis 37, so she is Israel. He mentions that Roman Catholics identify her as Mary. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/ Larkin argues nowhere in Scripture is the Church said to be a Mother, but it is prophesied of Israel. https://studylight.org/commentaries/clr/revelation-12.html GotQuestions agrees: the twelve stars are the twelve tribes, so the woman is Israel. https://www.gotquestions.org/Revelation-chapter-12.html
- **The church (older Protestant):** Matthew Henry reads the woman as the church, "clothed with the sun, justified, sanctified, and shining by union with Christ", with the twelve stars as the apostles' gospel teaching.  Gill (Baptist) sees the sun as Christ's righteousness worn like a garment.  Another commentator on the same page calls the Catholic reading "idle" and asks "when did she flee into the wilderness?" https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/12-1.htm
- **Neither view settled (Cambridge Bible):** It says the two common answers, Mary and the Church, are neither quite satisfactory. It adds that church considerations shouldn't rule out Mary being intended.  (same URL)
- **Catholic:** Akin says the woman has four meanings at once: Israel, the Church, Eve and Mary. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/the-woman-of-revelation-12 Another Catholic Answers page says the primary and literal sense is Mary, the mother of Jesus, and links this to her Assumption. https://www.catholic.com/bible-navigator/assumption-of-mary/rev121-5 A Catholic Answers video adds a link from 11:19: the ark of the covenant appears just before the woman, and "The ark is the Blessed Virgin Mary." https://www.catholic.com/video/proving-mary-was-raised-to-heaven-using-only-the-bible

**v. 2**
- Guzik: the birth pains are Israel's suffering under Roman occupation when Jesus was born. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- One Bible Hub commentator reads the pains as Old Testament believers' ardent longings for the promised Redeemer. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/12-1.htm
- Akin: Mary felt no literal pain at the birth, but she suffered in another sense when a sword pierced her heart at the cross. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/the-woman-of-revelation-12

**v. 3**
- Guzik: the dragon is a picture of Satan's character. The crowns are his false claim to be king. He quotes Walvoord, who sees the revived Roman Empire in the heads and horns. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- Wesley: the diadems show that though fallen, he was a great potentate still, even the prince of this world. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/12.htm
- Kelly: the seven heads mean complete ruling authority. The dragon has ten horns while the woman has twelve stars.  https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/12-17.html

**v. 4**
- Guzik: many take the swept-away stars to be a third of the angels who joined Satan's rebellion. Herod's killing of the infants first fulfilled the attempt to "devour" the child. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- Wesley reads it differently. The tail is "His falsehood and subtilty" and "a third" means simply a very large number. The dragon wants to stop Christ's kingdom from spreading.  https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-12.html
- Larkin traces Satan's efforts to stop the birth of Christ and then to kill him before the cross.  https://studylight.org/commentaries/clr/revelation-12.html

**v. 5**
- Almost everyone agrees the child is Christ (Psalm 2:9).
- Guzik: the verse names the start of Jesus' work (his birth) and its end (his return to rule). The child cannot be born of the church, because Jesus gives birth to the church. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- Wesley: this is Christ, considered not in his person, but in his kingdom, and he is "caught up" utterly out of his reach. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/12.htm
- One commentator on Bible Hub (unnamed in the excerpt) holds that the messiah here is not the son of Mary but simply born in the messianic community. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/12-1.htm

**v. 6 (strongest disagreement)**
- **Future (dispensational):** Guzik puts the 1,260 days in Daniel's 70th week, with our whole present age falling between v. 5 and v. 6. He mentions the Petra theory. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/ Preceptaustin says she flees at the middle of The 70th Week of Daniel. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/63774/ GotQuestions says possibly to Petra. https://www.gotquestions.org/Revelation-chapter-12.html
- **Church history:** Wesley (Methodist) places the wilderness in Europe and dates the 1,260 days from 847 to 1524.  https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/12.htm Barnes reads it as the true church kept safe during the corruptions of the papacy and the darkness of the middle ages. Clarke ties it to heresies spreading after Christianity became the empire's religion.  https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/wes/revelation/12-6.html
- **Reformed:** Ligonier argues that in Revelation the 1,260 days stand for the whole time between Christ's first and second comings. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman
- **Against the Mary reading:** Larkin says she flees into the wilderness, not Egypt as Mary did, and without her child.  https://studylight.org/commentaries/clr/revelation-12.html

**vv. 7–8**
- Guzik places this war in the middle of the Tribulation and says that until then Satan still has access to heaven. He argues at length that Michael is not Jesus, against the Seventh-day Adventist and Jehovah's Witness view. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- Preceptaustin: before this battle the dragon had access to heaven as he does in our day. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/63774/

**v. 9**
- Guzik: the five titles (dragon, ancient serpent, devil, Satan, deceiver) show him as vicious, an accuser, an adversary and a deceiver. "Devil" comes from a Greek word meaning "to slander."  https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- Bible.org (Constable-style notes): he is thrown down in the middle of the Tribulation. https://bible.org/seriespage/angelic-conflict-rev-121-17

**v. 10**
- **Future:** Guzik says Satan's accusing ends only at this point, which is why believers need Christ as advocate now.  https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- **Already at the cross:** Ligonier says that after failing to destroy Christ, Satan has already been thrown out. He can no longer accuse believers, who are clothed in Christ's righteousness. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman
- **In between:** Bible.org (Utley) notes Satan is cast out yet still accuses, so His power is broken, but he is still active. https://bible.org/book/export/html/21458
- Gill argues the song is sung by the saints in heaven, not by angels, because angels never call people "brethren."  https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/amp/revelation/12-10.html

**v. 11**
- Ellicott: better translated "on account of" the blood. Their victory is "owing to" the blood of the Lamb. https://biblehub.com/revelation/12-11.htm
- Spurgeon (Baptist): "The blood of the Lamb will not help us until it becomes our own", and the saints' testimony is a testimony concerning the blood of the Lamb.
- Coffman quotes Beasley-Murray: Satan's defeat came "not through Michael, but through the power of the sacrifice of Christ." https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/12-11.html
- Barnes: Christ won the victory by his death, and we triumph by the strength of that victory.  https://biblehub.com/commentaries/revelation/12-11.htm

**v. 12**
- Barnes: Satan's anger burns hotter because he knows that his time is limited. People's New Testament: the "woe" is Not an imprecation but a prediction. https://www.studylight.org/bible/eng/asv/revelation/12-12.html
- Wesley believed he was living in that "little time" himself.  https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/12.htm

**v. 13**
- Wesley: once Satan could no longer accuse the saints in heaven, he turned his wrath to do all possible mischief on earth. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/wes/revelation/12.htm
- Ligonier: the woman here is faithful Israel, the remnant of God's people. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman

**v. 14**
- Ligonier: the eagle's wings recall God carrying Israel through the wilderness in the Exodus (Exodus 19:4). "A time, and times, and half a time" equals the 1,260 days. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman
- Wesley: the great eagle is the Roman empire; the two wings, the eastern and western branches. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/wen/revelation-12.html
- Larkin takes it as a literal 3½ years.  https://studylight.org/commentaries/clr/revelation-12.html

**vv. 15–16**
- Ligonier: in Revelation the mouth usually stands for speech. So the flood may be slander from outside the church or false teaching from inside it. The earth swallowing it is a picture of defeat (Exodus 15). https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman
- Kelly: "the earth" means what was under settled government at this time. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/12-17.html
- Preceptaustin: the chase may be a continuation of the Beast's invasion of the glorious land. https://www.preceptaustin.org/revelation-12-commentary

**v. 17**
- **Jewish believers (dispensational):** Preceptaustin says "the rest of her children" should not be taken as spiritual offspring. They are physical descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/63774/ Guzik's list instead calls them Gentiles who come to faith during the Tribulation. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/revelation-12/
- **All God's people:** Ligonier calls them another picture of God's people. https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/the-dragon-pursues-the-woman
- **Christians:** Akin argues they are Christians, which is one reason the woman also stands for the Church. https://www.catholic.com/magazine/print-edition/the-woman-of-revelation-12
- Clarke reads the dragon as the pagan party, angry that its attempt to destroy Christianity failed.  Coffman: this is not an intensification of Satan's wrath, but an extension of it. https://www.studylight.org/commentary/revelation/12-17.html

**Modern scholarship (only a little found):** GotQuestions notes that scholars generally see Revelation 12 as an example of the ancient "combat myth motif". https://www.gotquestions.org/Satan-dragon.html
